gloss: quite a struggle; a hard time

definitions.gloss: quite a struggle; a hard time; a real effort
definitions.explanation: Describes a task or situation that requires considerable effort or trouble. Used when something turns out to be more difficult than expected.

examples.japanese: {駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}を{見|み}つけるのが{一苦労|ひとくろう}だった。
examples.english: Finding a parking spot was quite a struggle.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{毎朝|まいあさ}{起|お}こすのも{一苦労|ひとくろう}だ。
examples.english: Just waking the kids up every morning is a real effort.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{家具|かぐ}を{三階|さんがい}まで{運|はこ}ぶのは{一苦労|ひとくろう}だ。
examples.english: Carrying large furniture up to the third floor is quite a task.

notes:
USAGE:
Typically used with だ or だった to describe a completed or ongoing difficulty. The pattern ～のは{一苦労|ひとくろう}だ (doing X is quite a struggle) is very common. Despite the literal meaning of "one hardship," it emphasizes that something is unexpectedly troublesome.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～のは{一苦労|ひとくろう}だ (doing X is quite a struggle)
- {一苦労|ひとくろう}する (to have a hard time)
- {一苦労|ひとくろう}も{二苦労|ふたくろう}も (not just one but many hardships)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {苦労|くろう}: hardship, trouble — broader and more general, not limited to a single difficult task
- {手間|てま}: effort, bother — focuses on the time and labor required rather than difficulty
